_not: Harita 2 (The Drowned Reach) olayları, hazineleri ve kasaba hikâyeleri (campaign-dev 2026-10-25, maps-2-3.md 3.2 / 3.4; oyun içi metin İngilizce). Biçim data/campaign/events.json ile aynı (events{} choices[] şablonu, treasures{}, stories{}); src/campaign/data.ts iki dosyayı birleştirir, anahtarlar dr_ önekli (çakışmasın). Faction (M-L: dr_guild_hall, dr_monks_isle), Charter a ship (M-J: dr_ferry_office) ve Lighthouse (M-M: dr_lantern_rock) kurallı (campaign-dev 2026-10-27, src/campaign/reach.ts): seçenek alanları faction / needFaction / charter / light / gift, olay alanı again. Ödül sayıları PROVİZYON.

dr_quest_registry._not: A5 Undead görevi (dr90). "Let it drown": görev ödülsüz kapanır (Ömer A5 = a).
dr_quest_registry.title: The Drowned Registry
dr_quest_registry.text: Maredh's clerks wrote down every soul that drowned in the Reach. Your Undead finds a page with a name it has not heard in a hundred years, and the ink is still wet. Something in the court does not want it read aloud.

choices.label: Speak the name
choices.hint: Your Undead's quest. Read the name aloud and face what guards the page.
choices.result: The name rings off the drowned stone, and the guardians of the registry crumble to silt. Your Undead closes the book. It remembers now.

choices.label: Let it drown
choices.hint: Close the book and leave the name to the water. The quest ends here, without its reward.
choices.result: Your Undead closes the book and lets the water have it. Some names are better left unspoken.

dr_quest_roost._not: A5 Archer görevi (dr91): sınav savaşı kazanılınca açılan pencere (unvan ve bonus çipi sahnede quests.json'dan).
dr_quest_roost.title: The Gull Roost
dr_quest_roost.text: The last crossbowman tumbles from the ledge and the cliff-hunters cheer. They tie the Gull Feather to your Archer's bow: for one spring at least, the best eye on the Wreck Cliffs belongs to your company.

dr_quest_debt._not: A5 Cutthroat görevi (dr92). "Pay what you owe" da tam ödül (Ömer A5 = a).
dr_quest_debt.title: Rat's Nest
dr_quest_debt.text: A chalk mark on a door in Chandlers' Row: the sign your Cutthroat swore never to see again. The Dock Rats remember an unpaid debt, and they have hired corsair knives to collect it.

choices.label: Pay what you owe
choices.hint: Your Cutthroat's quest. Settle the old debt in coin, and walk away clean.
choices.result: The Dock Rats count the coin twice and wipe the chalk from the door. Your Cutthroat walks out of Saltmere owing no one.

choices.label: Settle it the old way
choices.hint: Your Cutthroat's quest. Fight the collectors; no ultimate in your first 3 turns.
choices.result: The collectors will not be collecting again. Your Cutthroat takes back the purse they came for, and a little more.

dr_quest_table._not: A5 Gambler görevi (dr93). "Walk away": görev açık kalır, sonra dönülür (kafile yola çıkabilir; state.ts > canWithdraw).
dr_quest_table.title: The Dicing Hulk
dr_quest_table.text: A beached hulk where the corsairs dice for shares. The house never loses, because the house cuts the throats of winners. Your Gambler pushes a purse onto the table: "One throw. Mine."

choices.label: Lay the stake
choices.hint: Your Gambler's quest. Win the throw, then win the fight: the house keeps its back row empty. Win: double your stake.
choices.result: The house loses for the first time in living memory. Your Gambler sweeps the purse off the table and leaves the dice behind.

choices.label: Walk away
choices.hint: Leave the table for now. You can come back later.

dr_wayshrine._not: A1 Wayshrine: sınav kazanılınca açılan pencere (nimetin adı ve etkisi sahnede çip olarak side-content.json > wayshrines'ten eklenir).
dr_wayshrine.title: Wayshrine
dr_wayshrine.text: The trial is done. The old flame on the altar steadies and burns clear, and something of it stays with your company: a small blessing that will travel with you for the rest of the journey.

dr_floodplain_farms.title: The Flooded Fields
dr_floodplain_farms.text: Farmers wade through their drowned fields, carrying what they can to the high ground. "Reavers came up the river last night," one of them calls. "They took our boats, and they'll be back for the rest."

choices.label: Help the farmers
choices.hint: Fight the river reavers. Win: a chest and some gold.
choices.result: The reavers flee downriver without their plunder. The farmers press what they can spare into your hands.

choices.label: Move on
choices.hint: Keep to the road.
choices.result: You leave the farmers to their buckets. The river keeps rising behind you.

dr_stilt_hamlet.title: The Eel-Wives
dr_stilt_hamlet.text: Women in oilskin coats mend nets on the walkways between the stilt houses. They watch you the way they watch the water: patiently.

choices.label: Barter with them
choices.hint: Pay 30 gold. They trade you one item from their stores.
choices.result: The eldest weighs your coins in her palm, then fetches a bundle wrapped in eel-skin.

choices.label: Ask about the weir
choices.hint: Hear what the eel-wives know.
choices.result: "The weir-wyrm was small once," the eldest says. "Then the Tide started rising. Now it grows with the water. Fight it where the ground is dry, if you can find any."

choices.label: Move on
choices.hint: Walk on through the hamlet.
choices.result: You nod to the eel-wives and walk on along the creaking boards.

dr_smugglers_reeds.title: The Reed Toll
dr_smugglers_reeds.text: A boat noses out of the reeds and blocks the channel. Two more slide in behind you. "This water's ours," says the woman at the bow. "Pay the toll or swim."

choices.label: Pay the toll
choices.hint: Pay 40 gold. The smugglers let you pass.
choices.result: The smugglers count your coins and pole their boats aside. "Safe travels," one of them grins.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.hint: Fight the smugglers. Win: their chest and their gold.
choices.result: The smugglers' boats drift empty in the reeds. Their strongbox is yours.

dr_fishmarket.title: The Fishmarket
dr_fishmarket.text: Gulls scream over the stalls. Fishwives shout prices, sailors shout back, and everyone talks about the sea.

choices.label: Listen to the rumours
choices.hint: Hear what the harbour is saying.
choices.result: "Black sails off the isles again," a sailor mutters. "And the bells of the sunken court rang last night. My grandmother says they ring when a queen is crowned."

choices.label: Buy from a stall
choices.hint: Pay 25 gold for one item a sailor brought back from the isles.
choices.result: The sailor unwraps a bundle of oilcloth and lets you pick one thing from it.

choices.label: Move on
choices.hint: Leave the market.
choices.result: You push your way out of the crowd and back to the street.

dr_guild_hall._not: M-L Faction (maps-2-3.md 3.4): tek seçim, geri alınmaz (CampaignState.faction). Sonuçları: Harbor Fort eliti (Order -> Guild Enforcer Bastion, Guild -> Inquisitor-Captain Vell), Monk's Isle içeriği, tüccar stoğu ağırlığı, Ferry Office bedeli. again faction: 'Not yet' seçilirse meydana dönünce yeniden sorulur.
dr_guild_hall.title: Guild Hall and Inquisition House
dr_guild_hall.text:
On one side of the square stands the Guild Hall, its doors open, its clerks busy with the harbour's trade. On the other stands the Inquisition House of the Order of St. Brann, its doors shut, its windows barred.

The Harbor-Master's people watch you from one door, the Brother-Provost's from the other. Saltmere is a city of two masters, and every newcomer is asked which one they serve. Whatever you answer, the city will remember it.

choices.label: Stand with the Order
choices.hint: Final. The Guild's enforcer holds Harbor Fort against you. The monks of Monk's Isle open their doors to you. Merchants favour armour and relics. A ship to the isles costs gold.
choices.result: The Brother-Provost unbars the door himself and presses the Order's seal into your hand. Across the square, the Guild Hall's doors swing shut.

choices.label: Stand with the Guild
choices.hint: Final. The Inquisitor-Captain holds Harbor Fort against you. The monks of Monk's Isle will bar their gate. Merchants favour weapons and trinkets. The Ferry Office charters you a ship as a favour.
choices.result: Harbor-Master Rook shakes your hand in front of the whole square and writes your name in the Guild's ledger. Behind you, the Inquisition House stays shut.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.hint: Answer another day. You can come back to the square.
choices.result: You leave both doors behind you. Neither side looks pleased, but Saltmere can wait.

dr_ferry_office._not: M-J Charter a ship (maps-2-3.md 3.2 #38): deniz yollarını açar (CampaignState.sea), Black Caravel dolaşmaya başlar. Bedel faction'a göre (M-L): Guild = iyilik (bedava), Order ya da taraf yok = altın (cost PROVİZYON, open-questions 433). again charter: 'Not now' seçilirse ofise dönünce yeniden sorulur.
dr_ferry_office.title: The Ferry Office
dr_ferry_office.text: The ferry clerk turns the pages of a ledger thick with the names of ships that never came back. "No one sails to the isles for nothing," he says without looking up. "The Black Caravel takes one ship in three. Pay the Guild's price, or bring me the Guild's word, and a fishing boat will be waiting for you at Fisher's Landing."

choices.label: Charter a ship
choices.hint: Pay 60 gold. The sea lanes from Fisher's Landing to the isles open for the rest of this map.
choices.result: The clerk counts your coins twice and writes a name in the ledger. "Fisher's Landing. Look for the boat with the red sail."

choices.label: Call in the Guild's favour
choices.hint: Free, for friends of the Guild. The sea lanes from Fisher's Landing to the isles open for the rest of this map.
choices.result: The clerk sees the Guild's mark and closes his ledger. "Friends of the Harbor-Master sail free. Fisher's Landing, the boat with the red sail."

choices.label: Not now
choices.hint: Leave the office. You can come back to charter a ship later.
choices.result: The clerk does not look up as you leave. Ships come and go; so do travellers.

dr_lantern_rock._not: M-M Lighthouse (maps-2-3.md 3.2 #45): feneri yakmak bu haritada görüşü artırır (reach.lighthouse.visibility; CampaignState.lit).
dr_lantern_rock.title: Lantern Rock
dr_lantern_rock.text:
The old lighthouse is dark, its great lamp cracked and dry. Gulls nest in the lamp room. From the gallery you can see the whole coast: the cliffs, the wrecks, and far out in the grey, the drowned isles.

There is still oil in the cellar, and the wick can be trimmed. With a little work, the light could burn again.

choices.label: Light the lamp
choices.hint: For the rest of this map you see one stop further along every road.
choices.result: The lamp catches, sputters, and then burns steady. Its beam sweeps the cliffs and the water, and the coast ahead comes out of the dark.

dr_widows_watch.title: The Ship on the Rocks
dr_widows_watch.text: A merchant ship lies on the rocks below the widows' walk, her crew clinging to the rigging. The wreckers are already rowing out to her. One of them looks up at you and waves a purse. "There's enough for everyone, friend. Just look the other way."

choices.label: Save the ship
choices.hint: Fight the wreckers. Win: the grateful merchant's chest.
choices.result: The wreckers' boats burn on the beach. The merchant's crew climbs ashore, and the captain opens his chest for you.

choices.label: Take the wreckers' cut
choices.hint: Take 50 gold and look the other way.
choices.result: The purse is heavy. Behind you the sea takes the ship, and the wreckers take the rest.

dr_saltspray_shrine.title: The Saltspray Shrine
dr_saltspray_shrine.text: A small shrine to the sea stands on the cliff, its stones white with salt. Old offerings lie in its niches: shells, fish-hooks, a child's shoe. The spray reaches it even on calm days.

choices.label: Leave an offering
choices.hint: The living recover 15% health.
choices.result: You leave a coin in the niche. The spray is cold and clean on your faces, and for a moment the wounds sting less.

choices.label: Read the inscription
choices.hint: Read what is carved on the shrine.
choices.result: The words are worn almost smooth. "To the Tide that gives and takes. Keep your half, as we keep ours." Someone has scratched a crown beneath it, split down the middle.

choices.label: Swear an oath
choices.hint: One hero swears an oath to the Tide: a lasting gift and a lasting price.
choices.result: The spray falls on the oath-taker's brow, and the Tide takes the words.

dr_monks_isle._not: M-L (maps-2-3.md 3.2 #56): Order tarafı = bedava dinlenme (heal = rest.heal 0,5) + relic (offhand hediye, VARSAYIM open-questions 433); Guild tarafı = savaş (2 Oathsworn + 2 Censer Monk) -> sandık; taraf yoksa eski ekmek seçeneği.
dr_monks_isle.title: Monk's Isle
dr_monks_isle.text: The monks of St. Brann keep a small house on the isle. Their bell rings for every ship that passes, and for every ship that does not come back.

choices.label: Accept the monks' bread
choices.hint: The living recover 20% health.
choices.result: The monks share their bread and their fire. They ask no questions, and they pray for you when you leave.

choices.label: Rest with the brothers
choices.hint: As friends of the Order: the living recover 50% health, and the abbot gives you a relic.
choices.result: The brothers wash the salt from your wounds and give you their beds. At dawn the abbot brings out a relic from the vault and puts it in your hands.

choices.label: Face the wardens
choices.hint: The monks know the Guild's mark. Fight 2 Oathsworn Brothers and 2 Censer Monks. Win: a chest.
choices.result: The wardens fall back behind their bell. You take what the Guild's enemies kept in their storehouse.

choices.label: Keep the vigil
choices.hint: Your Paladin's quest. Tonight the bell rings on its own and the drowned walk up the shingle toward it. Hold them off for 4 rounds.
choices.result: Dawn comes grey over the water, and the drowned slip back beneath it. Brother Aldo takes the bell-rope from your Paladin's hands and bows: "Brann kept this vigil once. Now you have kept it too."

choices.label: Move on
choices.hint: Thank the monks and sail on.
choices.result: You thank the monks and push off from their little jetty. The bell rings behind you.

dr_sunken_stair.title: The Sunken Stair
dr_sunken_stair.text:
A great stair of pale stone runs down from the last isle into the sea. The water stands back from it on both sides like a wall of green glass. At the bottom, far below, lights move in the windows of a drowned palace.

This is the way into the Sunken Court of Maredh. Whatever rules there, it is waiting.

dr_flooded_library.title: The Flooded Library
dr_flooded_library.text:
The court's library is knee deep in seawater, its books swollen past reading. But in a sealed case at its heart lies one dry book: a history of the court.

It tells how the founders of Valdoria carried the Ember of the First Hearth out of the mountain, and could not put it out. How they caged it in a crown and split the crown in two, one half to the mountain, one half to the sea, so that no single bearer could ever hold the whole fire. How the sea kept its half here, in Maredh, for four hundred years.

Your company makes camp among the shelves, on the one dry floor in the palace.

dr_two_crowns.title: Two Crowns
dr_two_crowns.text:
The Drowned Queen is gone. The Crown of Salt lies on the wet stones beside the Crown of Ash, and the two halves stir when you lift them, pulling at each other, pulling at your hands.

They pull north. Past Valdoria, past Morvane's burnt keep, toward the mountain where the fire was first dug out of the earth.

What was split must be mended, or ended.

dr_barge_wreck.title: Barge Wreck
dr_barge_wreck.text: The lurkers are dead. In the barge's flooded hold you find a sealed trader's chest.
dr_barge_wreck.reward: Open the chest to claim its gear and gold.

dr_ford_chapel._not: Cep (PROVİZYON): altın ağırlıklı, Raiders' Hoard gibi.
dr_ford_chapel.title: Chapel of the Ford
dr_ford_chapel.text: The villagers hid their savings in the chapel when the waters rose. They never came back for them.
dr_ford_chapel.reward: Take the savings: mostly coin, and one piece of gear.

dr_sunken_chapel.title: Sunken Chapel
dr_sunken_chapel.text: Beneath the bell tower, above the waterline, the chapel's treasury chest is still dry.
dr_sunken_chapel.reward: Open the chest to claim its gear and gold.

dr_eel_lair._not: Cep (PROVİZYON): az ama iyi, Sunken Shrine gibi.
dr_eel_lair.title: Eel-Mother's Lair
dr_eel_lair.text: The eel-mother's nest is built from the wrecks of boats, and the boats still hold their cargo.
dr_eel_lair.reward: Take the cargo: a few fine pieces of gear.

dr_crypt_stair._not: Cep (PROVİZYON): item ağırlıklı, Supply Wagons gibi.
dr_crypt_stair.title: The Crypt Stair
dr_crypt_stair.text: The old bishops were buried with their rings and their croziers. They will not miss them now.
dr_crypt_stair.reward: Take the grave goods: gear, and a little gold.

dr_smugglers_cave.title: Smugglers' Cave
dr_smugglers_cave.text: The smugglers' stash is piled at the back of the cave, above the high-tide line.
dr_smugglers_cave.reward: Open the stash to claim its gear and gold.

dr_sea_cave.title: Sea Cave Hoard
dr_sea_cave.text: The tide has carried the treasures of a hundred wrecks into this cave, and left the best of them high and dry.
dr_sea_cave.reward: Take the hoard: a few fine pieces of gear.

dr_monastery_vault.title: Salt Monastery Vault
dr_monastery_vault.text: The monks kept what the sea gave up in a vault beneath their house. They let you take what you need.
dr_monastery_vault.reward: Take what the monks offer: gear, and a little gold.

dr_salt_garden.title: The Salt Garden
dr_salt_garden.text: Among the salt flowers stands a coral casket, sealed with the court's crest.
dr_salt_garden.reward: Open the casket to claim its gear and gold.

dr_armory.title: Armory of Maredh
dr_armory.text: Most of the court's weapons have rusted to nothing, but a few were made to last.
dr_armory.reward: Take the best of the armory: a few fine pieces of gear.

dr_the_ferryman.title: The Ferryman
dr_the_ferryman.speaker: The Ferryman
dr_the_ferryman.text: An old ferryman sits on an upturned boat at the water's edge, splicing a rope with fingers like knotted roots. He looks a long while at the bundle in your pack before he looks at you.

dialogue.text: "Another lot come down the Long Stair. You walk like men with a coffin on your backs. Whatever is wrapped in that cloth, it's warm; I can feel it from here. Where are you taking it?"

choices.label: "To the sea. Lord Morvane's last words asked it of us."

dialogue.text: "Morvane. So the ash lord is dead, and his crown comes down my river. Then mind the Order. The monks of St. Brann have shut the road at Saltmere Gate. Quarantine, they call it. Nobody passes without a reason they like, and they like very few."

choices.label: "Who else crosses this river, besides us?"
"We'll give them a reason. Steel is a good one."

dialogue.text: "The water, same as the rest of us. Thirty years I've poled this ferry, and the river never ran backwards till this spring. Now the tide comes up as far as Reedgate, and some nights it brings the drowned with it. They climb the bank and stand there in the reeds, looking east. Will you still go on?"

choices.label: "We go on. Someone has to finish what Morvane began."
"For the right price, we'd go anywhere."

dr_the_ferryman.liked:
He knots off the rope and sets it down. "Then hear one thing more. That crown burns whoever calls on it, a little more each time. The keeper of the Cliff Chapel can wash the burn away; the monks taught her that much before they shut their gates."

"And take this. Someone left it on my boat and never came back for it. The river doesn't give much back, so see you keep it."
dr_the_ferryman.disliked: "Suit yourselves. The river doesn't care either way, and nor do I." He spits into the reeds and goes back to his rope.

epilogue.title: The Ferryman's Warning
epilogue.text:
He walks you down to the water and holds the boat steady against the reeds while you climb in. The crown's warmth bleeds through the cloth between you, and he watches it the way a man watches a fire he doesn't trust. "That burn it leaves. Ash in the blood; the monks call it the Ashen Taint. It doesn't fade when you sleep. It settles in, and it waits."

"So when it sits heavy on you, climb to the Cliff Chapel before you climb anywhere else. The keeper there washes it out and asks nothing for it. Tell her the ferryman sent you." He pushes off into the grey water. "And don't let the river keep you."

dr_weir_warden.title: The Weir-Warden
dr_weir_warden.speaker: Weir-Warden Ysolt
dr_weir_warden.text: Weir-Warden Ysolt keeps the sluice gates of Eelwick. She is soaked to the knees and has been for as long as anyone remembers, and she does not stop working while she talks.

dialogue.text: "You're bound for the Weir Mouth? Then listen, for I'll say it once. The wyrm is strong in the water and slow on the mud. On flooded ground its hide turns blades like oiled leather, and when it calls the flood in, it is twice the beast it was."

choices.label: "Then we strike it on dry ground, before the flood."
"We've killed bigger things than an eel."

dialogue.text: "Good. You think. Most who go down there only swing. Six of my wardens went to mend the broken weir last spring, and I pulled two of them out of the water. The wyrm holds the gap now, and every tide it grows fatter. Do you know why the water's rising?"

choices.label: "Tell us. We'd rather know than guess."
"What became of the two you pulled out?"

dialogue.text: "Because something under the sea is reaching for what you carry. My gates have held the marsh for twenty years, and this spring they groan every night. If the weir goes, Eelwick goes under with it. Will you clear the gap, or only pass through it?"

choices.label: "We'll clear it. Your gates will hold again."
"We pass through. Your gates are your own affair."

dr_weir_warden.liked:
For the first time she stops working. "Then go when the water's low, and hit it hard whenever it leaves the wet stone. When it calls the flood, don't waste your blows on it; wait for the mud."

"Take this. Eel-oil, and whatever else is in the bundle. It keeps the damp out of steel, and out of your bones, a little."
dr_weir_warden.disliked: "Hm. Then the weir will teach you, the way it teaches everyone." She turns back to her gates.

epilogue.title: The Weir-Warden's Gates
epilogue.text:
She walks you as far as the last sluice, where the water slaps the stone and the marsh smells of rot and iron. "Remember what I told you. That Slick Hide is the flood's gift, not its own. On wet stone your blades will slide off it. Out of the water it is only an eel with too many teeth, and an eel can be cut."

"If you clear the gap, I'll know it. The gates will stop groaning, and I'll sleep a night through for the first time since spring." She hauls the wheel round, and the sluice closes behind you with a long iron sigh. "Go on, then. The tide won't wait, and nor will I."

dr_harbor_master.title: The Harbor-Master
dr_harbor_master.speaker: Harbor-Master Rook
dr_harbor_master.text: Harbor-Master Rook meets you at the gate with two clerks and a ledger. He has heard of the company that brought down Lord Morvane, and by the look of him he has already worked out what you are worth, to the copper.

dialogue.text: "Welcome to Saltmere. You'll find everything here: Odo's Chandlery for supplies, the smithies by the quay, swords for hire at the barracks, a ship to the isles at the Ferry Office. Everything has a price. What brings you to the sea?"

choices.label: "The Tide. We mean to stop it."

dialogue.text: "The Tide. Hah. The Brother-Provost calls it a judgement, and he'd burn half the docks to prove it. The Guild calls it bad for trade, and we'd sooner drain the harbour than drown in it. Meanwhile the cathedral sinks a little further every week. Will you hear what the city has to offer, before you choose a side?"

choices.label: "We'll hear everyone out, the Provost too."
"What would the Guild want with a company like ours?"
"We don't take sides. We take coin."

dialogue.text: "Harbor Fort, for a start. It has changed hands twice this year, and whoever holds it holds the harbour mouth. Beyond that, the Black Caravel sinks one ship in three, and Admiral Vane takes a cut of every cargo that lives. The Order prays about it. The Guild would sooner see it ended. Can this city count on you?"

choices.label: "If the Caravel burns, the whole city gains. Count on that."
"Only for as long as it pays."

dr_harbor_master.liked:
Rook shuts the ledger with a soft clap. "A sensible company. Rare, in this town. Choose your side at the square when you're ready; I won't pretend I don't hope it's mine."

"Meanwhile, take this as a welcome from the Guild. We remember our friends, and we remember the ones who weren't."
dr_harbor_master.disliked: "Everyone takes a side in Saltmere, sooner or later." He closes his ledger. "Mind you don't take the wrong one."

epilogue.title: The Guild's Ledger
epilogue.text:
Rook walks you down to the quay himself, his clerks trailing behind. Out past the harbour mouth the walls of Harbor Fort squat on their rock, grey and patient. "Whoever holds that fort holds Saltmere by the throat. The Guild would very much like it held by friends."

"And somewhere beyond it the Black Caravel is turning on its circle, while Admiral Vane counts our cargo from his cove. The Order would pray him into the sea. The Guild would rather see him hanged and his debts settled, in that order." He taps the ledger under his arm. "Every name in here owes someone something. Mind yours stays on the right page."

dr_keepers_daughter.title: The Keeper's Daughter
dr_keepers_daughter.speaker: Keeper's Daughter
dr_keepers_daughter.text: The lighthouse keeper's daughter sits at the end of the jetty with a spyglass that is too big for her. She has watched the isles every day since her father's light went out, and she does not lower the glass when you come near.

dialogue.text: "You're crossing to the isles? Then watch for the black ship. Black sails, black hull. The Caravel. It sails a circle: the Sound, then the Narrows, then Open Water, then Storm Strait, and back to the Sound. Every time you move, it moves one stop."

"Captain Marrow. He laughs when he boards a ship, my father said, and he leaves nobody to tell of it. And behind him, in Gallows Cove, the Admiral. Admiral Vane. My father said the Admiral would never leave the cove while the Caravel still sails."

"He rowed out to Lantern Rock in the storm, the night the bells rang under the sea, to keep the lamp burning for the boats still out. The lamp went dark before morning, and he never came back. Mother says the sea keeps what it takes. Will you still cross?"

choices.label: "We'll cross. His watch is ours now."
"The isles won't wait on a dead man's lamp."

dr_keepers_daughter.liked:
She lowers the spyglass at last. "Then keep a light with you, the way he did, and keep your eyes on the black sails. Sink the Caravel and the Admiral will have to come out of his cove."

"Take this. It was his. He'd want it to go to the isles, even if he can't."
dr_keepers_daughter.disliked: "My father was right about the sea, whatever you think of him." She lifts the spyglass again and says nothing more.

epilogue.title: The Dark Lamp
epilogue.text:
She walks with you to the very end of the jetty and points the spyglass at a black stub of stone far out in the grey. "That's Lantern Rock. The lamp used to sweep the whole Sound, every night of my life. Then the storm came, and the bells rang under the water, and it went out. He went out with it."

"Mother says not to look for him. I don't, not really. I only look for the light." She folds the spyglass and holds it against her chest. "If you pass the Rock, look up at the lamp for me. Just once. Then come back and tell me what you saw."
